note: Known prediction divergences between the runtime (feat_math::fit + Model::predict) and one emitted lane, observed at the base commit of kernel2 PR 02 and read by crates/feat-math/tests/parity_bits.rs. An entry names the program, the lane (rust, python or cpp17-fitted), the input row id and both prediction bit patterns. The test fails on any divergence that is not listed here and on any listed entry that no longer reproduces. Entries are removed by the fix item they name, never regenerated to make the test pass.

entries.reason: Sign of a zero row sum. The runtime sums a row with Iterator::sum, which starts at -0.0, so a row of negative zeros has row_sum and row_mean -0.0; the fitted C++ row_sum loop starts at +0.0 and returns +0.0. sign(v ^ -1) turns that into a derived column of -4 in the runtime and +4 in the program, and the ridge prediction differs.

Non-finite input to a closed-form program. The runtime's closed-form predict evaluates the raw input, so NaN makes c0 + c1 + c2 + 1 non-finite and the prediction 0.0; the fitted C++ encode_row replaces a non-finite value with the zero fill first and predicts 1.25. Pipelines sanitize inputs in the runtime and agree. The artifact input contract (X4) decides the target behaviour.

Sign of a zero minimum or maximum. The fitted C++ lowers min and max to std::fmin and std::fmax; GCC treats them as commutative and may swap the operands before calling glibc, which returns its second argument when the two compare equal, so which zero comes back depends on the compiler's operand order. Here every term is -0.0 in the program (-40), while the runtime's f64::min and f64::max returned the second argument (-32).
